DRAFT-IETF-IDR-BGP-BFD-STRICT-MODE-10-1.note: Forbidden: a peer with strict-mode enabled whose BGP FSM is not enabled (stays Idle or never exchanges OPEN while BFD is not Up). TestSessionBFDStrictWithholdsKeepalive asserts, with bfd state Down and strict negotiated, session.State() == fsm.StateOpenSent after handleOpen, red on an FSM that held in Idle or refused the connection; TestSessionBFDStrictSendsKeepaliveOnBFDUp asserts the held session reaches OpenConfirm on BfdUp, so the enabled FSM is not parked in an unleavable state.

DRAFT-IETF-IDR-BGP-BFD-STRICT-MODE-10-2.note: Draft Section 10: "That is, BFD hold-down procedures MUST NOT prevent BGP from establishing a connection with the remote BGP speaker." The preceding sentence requires the FSM enabled, while the following paragraph permits Established to wait for hold-down. TestDraftBFDHoldDownDoesNotGateConnectionOrOPEN configures 400 ms, reads the actual local OPEN from an accepted connection, processes the remote OPEN/KEEPALIVE with an unadvanced FakeClock, and distinguishes Down pending from Up running hold-down. session_bfd_strict_test.go TestSessionBFDStrictWithholdsKeepalive and TestSessionBFDStrictEstablishesWhenPeerDoesNotAdvertise confine the gate to negotiated strict mode. Producers advanceAfterOpen and bfdStrictHolds gate KEEPALIVE/establishment, not the already observed TCP/OPEN exchange. Delaying connection/OPEN until hold-down elapsed or bypassing the hold-down assertion fails. This closes the old zero-hold-down fixture gap without demanding Established prematurely. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

DRAFT-IETF-IDR-BGP-BFD-STRICT-MODE-4-1.note: Draft Section 4 Event 35: "If BfdEnabled is FALSE, this event MUST NOT occur. When BFD has been disabled, the local system will trigger a BfdAdminDown event instead." session_bfd_strict.go raiseBFDStrictConfigChanged chooses AdminDown when disabled. All three carriers were read: session_bfd_strict_test.go TestSessionBFDStrictConfigChangedUsesConfigSubcode positively pins enabled Cease/Other Configuration Change and Idle; TestSessionBFDStrictConfigChangedWithBFDDisabled pins no event-side effect outside a pending substate; draft_ietf_idr_bgp_bfd_strict_mode_pending_test.go TestDraftBFDDisabledConfigChangeReleasesPendingSession now checks BOTH pending substates, exact OpenConfirm/Established state, cleared substate and an actual KEEPALIVE. Thus suppressing Event 35 without substituting AdminDown fails rather than satisfying only the first sentence. The enabled/disabled inputs differ in the governing condition, and no unrelated malformed UPDATE confounds the outcome. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

DRAFT-IETF-IDR-BGP-BFD-STRICT-MODE-6-1.note: Forbidden: a strict-mode speaker sending an OPEN without capability 74. TestBFDStrictCapabilityInSentOpen builds peers from configuration and counts code-74 TLVs in the octets sendOpen writes: exactly one with bfd strict, zero with strict under a disabled bfd block and with a bfd block without strict. Red if sendOpen drops or duplicates 74 or emits it without strict-mode enabled. The settings-level units remain as supporting evidence.
